hypotheses.title: Compute-side execution limit
hypotheses.statement: A compute-side ceiling materially contributes to the end-to-end performance symptom.

evidence_rules.interpretation: A lower compute ceiling is a model-side signal, not proof of runtime saturation.

discriminating_measurements: Precision/sparsity-matched achieved FLOP/s and peak over the same interval
Kernel-scoped Tensor/SM active cycles and instruction mix
Request-correlated kernel duration and serving latency
what_would_support: A controlled compute-relevant intervention changes the targeted kernel metric and end-to-end metric at fixed workload.
what_would_weaken: A validated compute intervention changes kernel execution but not the serving symptom.

hypotheses.title: Memory bandwidth limit
hypotheses.statement: DRAM bandwidth or memory-system behavior materially limits the target workload.

evidence_rules.interpretation: A memory-side roofline ceiling is a modeled ceiling, not proof that achieved traffic is on the critical path.

discriminating_measurements: Same-boundary DRAM read/write bytes and peak bandwidth
L2 hit rate, cache reuse and memory-stall counters
Kernel-scoped memory throughput aligned to request phases
what_would_support: A controlled memory-system intervention changes measured memory stalls/bandwidth and serving performance.
what_would_weaken: Memory traffic and stalls are low or unchanged during the symptom under a complete aligned capture.

hypotheses.title: Inter-GPU communication critical path
hypotheses.statement: Collective communication or fabric contention lies on the critical path.

evidence_rules.interpretation: Per-link activity is an observation; critical-path attribution also needs collective timing and topology.
Missing link counters are unknown, not evidence of no communication cost.

discriminating_measurements: Per-link directional traffic and matched capacity
Collective operation duration and wait time by rank
Communication/computation overlap on a mapped common clock
Physical/logical topology and routing/placement
what_would_support: A communication intervention reduces collective critical-path time and improves the serving metric.
what_would_weaken: Collective time is not on the critical path or communication reduction has no serving effect.

hypotheses.title: KV-cache capacity or allocator pressure
hypotheses.statement: KV-cache capacity, allocation, fragmentation, eviction or preemption contributes to decode degradation.

evidence_rules.interpretation: Occupancy alone does not establish allocation pressure or eviction.
Absence of a matched used/capacity pair leaves pressure unknown.

discriminating_measurements: Used/capacity bytes or tokens at matched scope
Allocator block allocation, fragmentation, eviction and preemption events
Request-correlated decode stalls and TPOT/ITL
what_would_support: A controlled cache capacity/allocator change alters eviction or stall events and improves decode metrics.
what_would_weaken: A complete matched capture shows no allocator pressure or request-correlated stalls.

hypotheses.title: Runtime scheduling or queueing
hypotheses.statement: Queue wait, batch formation, CPU dispatch or kernel gaps contribute to latency.

evidence_rules.interpretation: Serving metrics alone do not isolate the runtime mechanism; the candidate is explicitly not attributed.

discriminating_measurements: Request arrival, queue wait and batch formation timestamps
CPU scheduling, dispatch and synchronization traces
Kernel launch gaps and phase-aligned active duration
Offered load, achieved throughput and request mix
what_would_support: A scheduler intervention changes the targeted wait component and end-to-end latency at comparable offered load.
what_would_weaken: Queue and dispatch components are negligible or their controlled reduction does not improve latency.

hypotheses.title: Thermal or power throttling
hypotheses.statement: Active thermal or power throttling contributes to the performance symptom.

evidence_rules.interpretation: Only throttle-active counters indicate reported throttling; temperature or power alone is insufficient.

discriminating_measurements: Throttle-active reason counters and clocks over time
Power, temperature and cooling conditions
Kernel and serving metrics on the same time axis
what_would_support: A safe, controlled change to thermal/power conditions changes throttle activity and performance.
what_would_weaken: Validated throttle counters remain inactive during the symptom and no related clock/power event occurs.
